title: When you land
body:
The Yamagata Shinkansen "Tsubasa" runs direct from Tokyo Station to Yamagata Station, about 2h22m at its fastest (up to ~2h45m on slower services), roughly hourly.

Every seat on Tsubasa is reserved — there is no unreserved car (JR East dropped it in spring 2022). Book all 8 seats together well ahead so the group sits as a block. ⚠ The reserved-seat fare is ≈¥11,450 one-way in an ordinary car (¥6,050 base fare + ¥5,400 express charge) — confirm the exact figure at booking (eki-net.com) or a ticket window.

No oversized-baggage reservation is required on this Shinkansen network (unlike the Tokaido/Sanyo/Kyushu lines) — storage is first-come, first-served overhead or behind the last row, so board together and claim space as a group.

title: Local essentials
body:
Carry cash for this trip — more than a Tokyo itinerary would need. The Hanagasa Bus to Ginzan Onsen is cash-only (¥1,000/adult, no IC card), and Ginzan Onsen itself has no convenience store or ATM in town (nearest is ≈30 min by car); several ryokan there don't take cards.

Suica/IC coverage thins out fast once you leave central Yamagata city. ⚠ Multiple Japanese sources agree Ōishida Station (the gateway to Ginzan Onsen) doesn't accept IC cards, though this couldn't be confirmed against JR East's own site — buy a paper ticket or plan to pay cash there regardless.

7-Eleven and Japan Post ATMs in Yamagata city itself accept foreign cards normally.

title: Entry & documents
body:
This guide assumes US passports for the whole party — see the Trip kit's entry card. If anyone travels on a different passport, their exemption length may differ (commonly 15, 30, 90, or 180 days depending on nationality); check Japan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs list directly.

Japan's "Visit Japan Web" pre-registration (customs declaration + optional tax-free shopping registration) is a genuinely useful but optional step before arrival — ⚠ not independently re-confirmed as still current for Oct 2026. No new ESTA-style pre-clearance system applies to this trip; Japan's proposed "JESTA" system isn't due before fiscal year 2028.

title: Phone & data
body:
eSIMs (Ubigi, Japan Wireless and others) and airport pocket-wifi/SIM counters both work well for this trip. Docomo has the deepest rural coverage in Tohoku, so a multi-network eSIM or a Docomo-backed one is the safer pick outside Yamagata city.

Coverage in Ginzan Onsen's mountain-valley setting wasn't independently tested — expect it to be adequate but not tested to the same standard as the cities.

title: Booking checklist
body: The Ginzan Onsen overnight is the one genuinely time-critical booking on this trip — start today.

checklist.text: Book the Ginzan Onsen overnight ryokan (Ginzanso is the primary pick — 40 rooms/≈200 guests, the only property realistically sized for a group of 8 in one booking; Takimikan and Showakan are backups)
checklist.note: Comparable Ginzan Onsen ryokan release reservations ≈3 months ahead — for Oct 20-23, 2026 that window opened around Aug 1, 2026, so this is already time-critical as of this research pass (2026-08-28). Call Ginzanso directly (0237-28-2322) as well as checking online.

checklist: Reserve all 8 Tsubasa Shinkansen seats together, Tokyo → Yamagata (every seat is reserved — no unreserved car)
Reserve the Yonezawa Beef Tokiwa private room (up to 14 guests) for the group dinner — phone 023-666-4433 or TableCheck online
